change.title: pr-80528-flat
change.description: ref(crons): Reorganize incident creation / issue occurrence logic
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: schedule_type display rewrite is computed and then discarded
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor.config`, rewrites `schedule_type` to its display name (lines 160-163), but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (line 168), so the copy is never read. The `get_schedule_type_display()` call is wasted work. The payload keeps the raw integer: `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:119` asserts `"schedule_type": 2` in `contexts.monitor.config`. Either delete lines 160-163 to match the pinned output, or return `config` and update that assertion. The second option changes the event payload, so decide which is intended. The code was moved verbatim from mark_failed.py, so this is not a regression.
findings.originReason: The base get_monitor_environment_context in mark_failed.py has the same discarded copy; the PR only moved it.

verification.reason: `config` is copied and its `schedule_type` rewritten at lines 160-162, but line 168 returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so the copy is never used. The test at test_mark_failed.py:119 expects the raw value 2. This code is identical in the base mark_failed.py.

findings.title: Typo in get_failure_reason docstring
findings.body: "humam readible" should read "human readable". Trivial, but the line is new in this file.
findings.originReason: The typo is already in the base mark_failed.py docstring.

verification.reason: Line 132 of the docstring says "humam readible". The same typo is at base mark_failed.py:300, and the PR moved it unchanged.

findings.title: Can the ERROR branch reach the occurrence guard with no active incident?
findings.body: In the `MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch, `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` (line 84). `active_incident` returns None when no open incident exists (src/sentry/monitors/models.py:714-724). The guard at line 92 (`and incident`) then skips the occurrence with no log, while `try_incident_threshold` still sends `monitor_environment_failed` and returns True. Is status ERROR with no open MonitorIncident reachable, for example after an incident is resolved while status is stale? If it is, a failed check-in produces no occurrence and no trace. The logic is unchanged from mark_failed.py, so this is a question for the author, not a regression in this PR.

verification.reason: The described mechanics hold: active_incident returns None when no open incident exists (models.py:719-724), and the guard at incidents.py:92 then skips the occurrence without logging while the signal is still sent. The code alone can't show whether status ERROR with no open incident is actually reachable. The logic is identical to base mark_failed.py:173-191.

contracts.action: mark_failed hands the failed check-in to the incident path
contracts.before_after: Same arguments and body. Only the function name changed (mark_failed_threshold to try_incident_threshold) and the code moved modules.
contracts.visible_effect: None. Incident creation, status change and occurrence production happen exactly as before.

contracts.action: One issue-platform occurrence produced per check-in in previous_checkins
contracts.equivalent_path: Base src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py loop calling create_issue_platform_occurrence (now create_incident_occurrence in src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:28-113)
contracts.before_after: Identical loop and arguments. The base code also produced one occurrence per previous check-in.
contracts.visible_effect: With failure_issue_threshold N, the transition to ERROR produces up to N occurrences with the same fingerprint. The tests expect this (tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:299-300 expects threshold calls).
contracts.failure_mode: src/sentry/issues/producer.py:79-90 catches KafkaException, logs it and drops the occurrence, which is visible only in logs. Other exceptions raised by produce_occurrence_to_kafka propagate out of mark_failed. Whether the callers handle them is not confirmed.
contracts.open_question: Do the monitor consumer and clock tasks catch exceptions raised from mark_failed, or does a non-Kafka error abort the batch? This is pre-existing and not changed by this PR.

contracts.action: Look up the last successful check-in for the evidence row
contracts.before_after: Identical. The query runs once per occurrence, so it is repeated for each check-in in the threshold loop.
contracts.visible_effect: The Last successful check-in evidence row shows the isoformat timestamp or Never.
contracts.failure_mode: A database error propagates. There is no fallback, and the occurrence is not produced.

contracts.action: Build contexts.monitor on the occurrence event
contracts.before_after: Identical, including the unused config rewrite (see finding at line 160).
contracts.visible_effect: The event's contexts.monitor.config carries the raw schedule_type integer, not the display name. The test pins this (tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:114-123).

summary: This part is a relocation. `mark_failed_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` moved from src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py into src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py and src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py. They were renamed to try_incident_threshold and create_incident_occurrence, and SimpleCheckIn moved to src/sentry/monitors/types.py. The moved bodies match the base code. The lazy imports the tests patch through (sentry.issues.producer.produce_occurrence_to_kafka) still work, and no remaining code imports the old names. Findings: an unused config rewrite whose test pins the raw value (consider), a docstring typo (consider), and a question about an ERROR status with no active incident silently skipping the occurrence, which predates this change (question). I found no blocker and no regression.
